note: Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) explicitly report 16 of 19 individuals with HSP phenotype and longer survival, versus 3 of 19 presenting with severe hypotonia.

evidence.text: The study describes 19 affected individuals with NFU1 missense variants where 16/19 present with early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) with longer survival and 3/19 present with neurodevelopmental delay and severe hypotonia.

source.title: Phenotypic continuum of NFU1-related disorders - PubMed
source.quote: We report 19 affected individuals from 10 independent families with ultra-rare bi-allelic NFU1 missense variants associated with a spectrum of early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) phenotype with a longer survival (16/19) on one end and neurodevelopmental delay with severe hypotonia (3/19) on the other.

evidence.text: The primary paper by Kaiyrzhanov et al. establishes the phenotypic continuum of NFU1-related disorders between MMDS1 and HSP across 19 patients.

source.title: Phenotypic continuum of NFU1‐related disorders
source.quote: NFU1 missense variants associated with a phenotype ranging from early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia
